views.label: Input to display
views.note: Player input becomes a command; the Model updates state; the View renders that state.

views.label: Controller prompts
views.note: Describe input methods, action mapping, selection, editing and actions allowed in each state.

views.label: Model prompts
views.note: Describe objects, properties, consequences, timing, simulation states and reset rules.

views.label: View prompts
views.note: Describe the camera, reference artwork, proportions, layout, sound and visible feedback.

cards.title: Start Here — My Game Brief
items: My game is called: ___. The player can: ___. The player's goal is: ___.
The setting is: ___. First ___, then ___, finally ___.
Build first: ___, ___ and ___. Save for the next version: ___.
I will be happy when I can see or do: ___. Choose one playable scene to check first.
This is a planning template drawn from Logan's three games; it is not a claim about their exact source-code architecture.

cards.title: Model — Fill In the World and Rules
items: Objects and properties: What exists? ___. What values can change? ___.
Cause and effect: If ___ happens, ___ should happen. Different objects react like this: ___.
States: Before Start ___; while Running ___; after Finish ___.
Timing and progression: First ___, then ___, finally ___. How quickly should it happen? ___.
Goal and reset: Success means ___. Restart restores ___. Changing a location restores ___.

cards.title: View — Fill In Appearance and Feedback
items: Camera: The player sees the world from ___. Structures need this depth: ___.
Visual reference: Match ___. Three details that make it look right: ___, ___ and ___.
Colors and scale: Materials/colors ___. People, boats and buildings are proportioned like ___.
Layout: Selector ___. Main scene ___. Controls ___. Tools/palette ___.
Motion, sound and visibility: The player should see ___ and hear ___. Important objects must remain visible when ___.

cards.title: Controller — Fill In Player Interaction
items: Input methods: Keyboard / buttons / click / touch / drag: ___.
Action mapping: When I press or use ___, send the command to ___.
Selection and placement: Choose ___, then ___ to place or change it.
Editing tools: ___ changes ___. Cancel or undo works like ___.
Allowed actions: In Ready ___; in Running ___; in Finished ___. Start, Finish and Restart send these commands: ___.

cards.title: Driving — MVC Example
items: Controller: Arrow keys or WASD and on-screen direction buttons steer the player car; Restart requests a new run.
Model: Drive for as long as possible. Buildings remain intact after collisions; trees fall; serious crashes respawn the car nearby. Water blocks driving.
View: A 3D follow camera shows hills, city streets and coastline, with detailed scenery and visible collision effects.
Check: Hit a tree and keep driving; crash into a building and reappear near the crash. Compare scenery against the chosen picture.

cards.title: Earthquake Simulator — MVC Example
items: Controller: Select one landmark; Start, Finish, Smaller and Bigger request simulation actions.
Model: Ready / Running / Finished; light shaking sways the structure, sustained strong shaking damages it; occupants and traffic evacuate gradually. Finish preserves the result; Start rebuilds.
View: A recognizable landmark dominates the scene, with detailed surrounding housing, varied cars, an alarm and readable progressive collapse.
Check: Show swaying before collapse, gradual evacuation, a frozen result after Finish and a rebuilt landmark on the next Start.

cards.title: Tsunami Simulator — MVC Example
items: Controller: Select Shanghai, New York or Hawaii; use the four simulation buttons; Pencil, Eraser and Hammer edit or damage the dam; select an entity then tap to place it.
Model: Waves overtop and weaken the dam; a breach accelerates flooding. Boats float or capsize, passengers swim, and rescue follows the wave sequence. Location selection restores a fresh scene.
View: A side camera reveals 3D buildings and dam, natural colors, small people and boats, cracks, splashes and visible underwater objects. Rubbish stays beside its bin.
Check: A taller dam blocks the same early wave; hammer damage opens the barrier; revisiting a city restores pristine defaults; faster floodwater reaches buildings sooner.

cards.title: One Feature, Three Responsibilities
items: Bigger button — View: its label, size, color and screen position.
Bigger button — Controller: a press sends an increase-size command.
Bigger button — Model: wave size changes within bounds and affects future waves.
The Controller requests an action; the Model decides the outcome; the View makes that outcome visible.

cards.title: Update Template — Keep Each Change Clear
items: Change: ___. What happens now: ___. What I want instead: ___.
Model: What rule, state or timing changes? ___. View: What looks, moves or sounds different? ___. Controller: What player action changes? ___.
Keep unchanged: ___. Priority: Now / Next / Optional. I can check it by: ___.
Example: Floodwater arrives too slowly. Change Model transport timing; check the View to see earlier arrival; keep the existing controls.
